newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ka Wah Bank plans rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Ka Wah Bank plans rights issue.

text.p: The Ka Wah Bank Ltd is planning a 19-for-100 rights issue to raise about HK$747.5 million, the company said in an announcement published on Monday.
The company said the rights issue would raise a minimum of HK$747.5 million and a maximum of HK$755.3 million before expenses with the funds raised used to expand the bank's capital base.
The issue price of HK$3.15 per rights share represented a discount of about 6.0 percent to the closing price of HK$3.35 on May 2, the announcement said.

The issue price was also a discount of 5.1 percent to the theoretical ex-rights price of approximately HK$3.32 per share. The company's major shareholder, China International Trust and Investment Corp which holds 61.3 percent of the issued share capital of the company, would take up its full allotment, the notice said.
The bank was currently operating well within its required capital adequacy ratio, but the company took a conservative approach to the maintenance of this ratio, it said.
Since 1986, the business of the company and its subsidiaries has expanded considerably, with net profit growing at an annual rate of more than 20 percent, the notice said.
An expansion of the company's capital base would create an important platform for the long-term development of its banking business, it said.
The issue was approved at the company's ordinary annual general meeting held on April 28. Rights shares were to be provisionally allotted to shareholders registered as at May 20, the notice said.
Trading in Ka Wah shares on an ex-rights basis will begin on May 16 and dealing in the shares and nil-paid rights would be between May 29 and June 6, the notice said.
